title: Find the value of an expression, not x
subtitle: Linear equations in one variable · 23 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **23 of the official questions in Linear equations in one variable are this one** — 17 Easy, 6 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- It says 'If [equation], what is the value of' followed by something other than x: 3x, x − 4, 2x + 1, or a multiple of the whole left side.
- The trap choices include the value of x.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) See whether the target expression is a multiple or shift of something already in the equation (for example, the target is half the left side, or equals the left side minus a constant).
- 2) If it is, get it in one move by dividing or subtracting on both sides.
- 3) If it isn't, solve for x and substitute.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Solve for x as in a bare equation, then type the target expression with that x value (or define x = value on one line and type the expression on the next).
It works, but it's slower than spotting the scaling.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You stop at x and choose it because it's listed.
The other traps are the value of an intermediate expression, or the result of scaling only part of the equation.

sections.heading: You are losing these
